name: img-stitch
desc: Free, open-source image stitcher for Windows — combine screenshots and photos into long images, aligned. 100 MB portable, offline, MIT.
features: ✅ **Vertical, horizontal and grid layouts** — long web captures, side-by-side comparisons and contact sheets
✅ **Overlap auto-alignment** — detects matching strips between sequential screenshots and seams them cleanly
✅ **Border and background control** — gap width, background color and rounded edges between tiles
✅ **Auto-crop overlap** — strips duplicated scroll regions instead of stacking them
✅ **Memory-safe large canvases** — stitches 50-plus images into a 30000 px result without exhausting RAM
✅ **Export presets** — web-optimized JPEG or lossless PNG at chosen scale
✅ **100 MB self-contained exe** — imaging codecs bundled, portable, offline, MIT with SHA-256 releases
compare: | Price | **Free, MIT** | Free, OSS | Paid | Freemium |
| Overlap trim for scrolls | **Yes** | No | Partial | Partial |
| 50-plus tile contact sheets | **Yes** | No | Partial | No |
| Portable, no install | **Yes, 100 MB** | Installer | Installer | Web |
faqQ: how to combine multiple screenshots into one long image?
faqA: Chat and webpage captures arrive as a dozen fragments with scroll overlaps, and pasting them into Paint produces visible seams. img-stitch finds the matching strips, trims duplicates and outputs one clean long image, or a bordered grid when you need a comparison sheet. It is a 100 MB portable exe, MIT, offline.
s1: Dark canvas (#121418, orange #F97316): 12 screenshot tiles in vertical order, seam markers green where overlap was trimmed, canvas height readout 18,420 px.
s2: Layout panel: vertical, horizontal and grid modes, gap slider at 8 px, background color swatch, auto-crop overlap toggle on.
s3: Export dialog: JPEG and PNG cards, scale selector 100 percent, memory estimate bar green, preview strip of the final seam.
